Replay

Immutable authored definitions

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use definitions.Store(Value) to retain immutable authored values across live state, history and checkpoints. It publishes bounded canonical values under a Ref containing semantic version, schema fingerprint and content checksum. Resource handles, nodes, strings, slices and pointers cannot enter Value. Reads return copies. The store owns allocations outside World; do not copy it or mutate its metadata/entries directly.

Odin
store: defs.Store(Weapon_Definition)
report := defs.init(&store, 16)
// Destroy also cleans up a failed init.
ref, report := defs.publish(&store, definition, GAME_CONTENT_VERSION)
value, found := defs.get(&store, ref)

Publication validates schema values, then an optional typed validator returning a Report. Failure preserves existing entries. Reports own bounded 256-byte path and message buffers, including after schema destruction; longer diagnostics are truncated. report_path/report_message borrow text from the report you supply. Repeat publication of identical canonical values reuses a reference; changed values or semantic versions produce distinct references. Padding is excluded. The fingerprint/checksum uses Replay's existing FNV codec, not cryptographic identity. A matching reference with different canonical bytes is rejected as a collision within the store. Authenticate imported content through the existing transport/admission layer; this API alone is not a trust boundary.

There is no automatic eviction. pin(ref) protects a version needed by live history, pending work or checkpoints; remove and destroy refuse pinned values. Call unpin after the last corresponding dependency ends. Multiple pins count independently. Pinning is explicit because the store cannot infer references hidden in arbitrary World layouts. Build/admit a complete dependency set before starting or restoring a simulation. Missing definitions must fail admission; do not silently substitute the latest revision.

Two valid approaches:

  • Embed baked values in World/checkpoints. Replay owns their lifetime naturally; no external lookup or store pin is needed after copying. Cavecrawl uses this.
  • Store only portable definition references in World and keep a frozen catalog available to the simulation step. Pin every version its retained history may read, and serialize/transfer those dependencies with checkpoints before allowing restore. Never hide mutable Resource data behind a reference to reduce history size.

The store uses bounded linear lookup; it is intended for definition catalogs, not per-entity hot loops. It allocates at initialization, and publication/read/pin operations allocate nothing internally. Schema and diagnostics retain their usual compiled-module lifetime. Access and callbacks must be serialized; callbacks must not mutate/reenter the same store.

Godot baking#

Baking converts authored Resource or scene data into immutable simulation values. scenegd.bake runs a typed extractor and publishes only after complete success. The source can be a Resource pointer, typed script value, or a fixed batch. The source is borrowed synchronously; it must stay alive during extraction. The output has the store's pointer-free canonical value type.

Odin
ref, report := scenegd.bake(&store, source, GAME_CONTENT_VERSION,
    proc(source: Source, ctx: ^scenegd.Bake_Context) -> Definition {
        root := scenegd.bake_scene2(ctx, source.scene, "$.scene")
        spawn, ok := scenegd.bake_marker2(ctx, root, "Markers/Spawn")
        count := scenegd.bake_int(ctx, source.count, 0, 32, "$.count")
        return Definition{spawn=spawn, count=u16(count)}
    })

The context retains the first error reported through bake_fail. Validate numbers before narrowing their types. Schema checks and an optional typed validator run before publication. Application rules such as collision geometry, wave limits and cross-field constraints remain explicit.

bake_scene2 owns temporary detached scene instances, destroying them on success and every failure path. The context supports at most 16 simultaneous scenes. Roots must be Node2D with identity transform. bake_marker2 accepts nested Node2D ancestry and composes local transforms into root-local coordinates; top-level ancestors and nonfinite positions are rejected. Detached extraction does not run _ready, but scripts/resources can still have constructors: use authored data scenes appropriate for loading. Do not free or retain a returned temporary node.

Presentation PackedScenes remain separately owned by the application. Retain them only after a successful bake and release old references when their presentations retire. Cavecrawl demonstrates atomic replacement of a two-floor definition set and its retained scenes. Resource edits after baking cannot mutate the values.

No reflection annotations or generator are required. The typed manual extraction keeps authored paths and game constraints visible and remains compile-checked on native and WASM targets. tests/replay_definitions covers store contracts; tests/replay_nodes exercises actual detached scene extraction and cleanup.

Canonical build artifacts#

artifact_export(&store, ref, source_digest) returns owned envelope bytes from an already validated immutable definition. artifact_import(&store, bytes, semantic, source_digest) validates exact schema, semantic contract, length, checksum and canonical values before publishing. An overload accepts a typed game validator. Passing source zero accepts any source digest; a nonzero value requires a match. Callers delete export bytes. This remains corruption detection, not authentication.

Artifacts reuse the canonical schema envelope with definition kind 0x4446 and file-format epoch 1. The metadata tick holds the optional authoring-source digest; it grants no authority and schedules no simulation work.

Scrapyard has one typed Godot extractor for interactive admission and explicit headless export. tools/stock.py invokes dev/export_content.tscn, records source hashes and verifies build provenance; it never interprets gameplay TRES fields. Its headless stock code decodes the committed artifact. Use --check in CI to reject changed nested resources or stale artifact/receipt pairs without Godot. See the complete authoring workflow.

The typed archetype registry associates these value contracts with separately owned local scenes. Evolution tools freeze revision dependencies and scaffold explicit conversions.
